{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/_imports.py\n@@\n def resolve_swift_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:\n-    \"\"\"Swift uses module-level imports — not resolvable to individual files.\"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"Best-effort local Swift import resolution.\n+\n+    Swift imports are usually module-level and often external. Resolve only when\n+    the import path clearly matches a local ``.swift`` file.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    text = import_text.strip()\n+    if not text:\n+        return None\n+\n+    module_path = text.replace(\".\", os.sep)\n+    leaf = module_path.split(os.sep)[-1]\n+    source_dir = os.path.dirname(source_file)\n+\n+    candidates = [\n+        os.path.join(source_dir, module_path + \".swift\"),\n+        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path + \".swift\"),\n+        os.path.join(scan_path, \"Sources\", module_path + \".swift\"),\n+        os.path.join(scan_path, \"Sources\", module_path, f\"{leaf}.swift\"),\n+        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path, f\"{leaf}.swift\"),\n+    ]\n+    seen: set[str] = set()\n+    for candidate in candidates:\n+        if candidate in seen:\n+            continue\n+        seen.add(candidate)\n+        if os.path.isfile(candidate):\n+            return candidate\n     return None\n*** End Patch\n"
}

> AGENT

Yes, this was a real fundamental issue, not just a one-off hang.

Root cause was twofold:
1. `next` was serializing huge cluster payloads into `query.json` (`auto/security` had 17,819 members), with repeated heavy metadata.  
2. `exclude` directory patterns were matching exact paths only, not descendants, so excluded trees like `.claude/worktrees` stayed in state.

I implemented both a tactical fix and a structural one:

- Bounded cluster serialization in `next` output so `query.json` doesn’t try to dump entire cluster members:
  - [output.py:11](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/next_parts/output.py:11)
- Removed per-item `plan_cluster.sibling_ids` duplication (high-cardinality repeated field):
  - [plan_order.py:53](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/plan_order.py:53)
- Fixed ignore matching so directory patterns suppress descendants:
  - [filtering.py:88](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_state/filtering.py:88)
- Added regression tests:
  - [test_direct_coverage_modules.py:359](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/test_direct_coverage_modules.py:359)
  - [test_suppression_scoring.py:199](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/state/test_suppression_scoring.py:199)

Validation:
- `desloppify next --count 1` now returns quickly (no timeout).
- `desloppify next --cluster auto/security --count 10` also returns quickly.
- `desloppify exclude .claude/worktrees` removed 16,510 findings immediately from state.

Are we losing important data?
- We are only trimming *query artifact payload* for cluster members (sample + counts), not scanner state.
- Core actionable data remains available via queue totals and `next --cluster ...` drill-in.
- This is the right tradeoff: avoid writing unbounded operational payloads while keeping full analysis in state.

So yes: this points to an over-collection problem, and the changes move it in the right fundamental direction.

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/query.py\n@@\n def _minimal_payload(payload: dict, *, max_bytes: int) -> dict:\n     \"\"\"Build a minimal fallback payload when budget cannot be met.\"\"\"\n@@\n     minimal[\"query_truncated\"] = {\n         \"mode\": \"minimal\",\n         \"max_bytes\": max_bytes,\n         \"items_sample\": len(sample_items),\n     }\n-    return minimal\n+    return _fit_payload_to_budget(minimal, max_bytes=max_bytes)\n+\n+\n+def _fit_payload_to_budget(payload: dict, *, max_bytes: int) -> dict:\n+    \"\"\"Shrink payload further until it fits max_bytes.\"\"\"\n+    trimmed = dict(payload)\n+\n+    items = trimmed.get(\"items\")\n+    if isinstance(items, list):\n+        keep = len(items)\n+        while keep > 0 and _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes:\n+            keep = max(0, keep // 2)\n+            trimmed[\"items\"] = items[:keep]\n+\n+    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes and \"config\" in trimmed:\n+        trimmed.pop(\"config\", None)\n+        trimmed[\"config_truncated\"] = True\n+\n+    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes and \"queue\" in trimmed:\n+        trimmed[\"queue\"] = {}\n+\n+    if _payload_size_bytes(trimmed) > max_bytes:\n+        return {\n+            \"command\": payload.get(\"command\"),\n+            \"query_truncated\": {\n+                \"mode\": \"minimal\",\n+                \"max_bytes\": max_bytes,\n+                \"overflow\": True,\n+            },\n+        }\n+\n+    query_meta = trimmed.get(\"query_truncated\")\n+    if isinstance(query_meta, dict) and isinstance(trimmed.get(\"items\"), list):\n+        query_meta[\"items_sample\"] = len(trimmed[\"items\"])\n+    return trimmed\n*** End Patch\n"

Also check for subscript writes: d[\"key\"] = val\n         for target in node.targets:\n             self._check_subscript_write(target, node.lineno)\n+        _mark_assignment_escape(self, node.targets, node.value)\n         self.generic_visit(node)\n*** End Patch\n"
